question: Which of the following formulas is used to determine the Gross Fiscal Deficit?

options.text: Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt creating Capital Receipts)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt creating Capital Receipts)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The formula used to determine the **Gross Fiscal Deficit** is **Total Expenditure - (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt creating Capital Receipts)**.
 
• This formula helps in understanding the gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue receipts along with non-debt creating capital receipts.
 
• It is a critical measure to assess the financial health of the government.
 
• Gross Fiscal Deficit indicates the** total borrowing requirements of the government**.
 
• It is an important metric for economic policy makers and analysts to gauge the sustainability of government finances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit** is a broader measure compared to budget deficit as it includes not just the shortfall in revenue but also the expenditure on capital outlays.
 
• Understanding fiscal deficit helps in planning effective fiscal policies to ensure economic stability and growth.
 
• Governments often finance their fiscal deficits through borrowing from domestic or foreign sources.
 
• High fiscal deficits can lead to higher public debt and interest rates, impacting the economy's overall health.
